profiles.meeting_scenario: A troubleshooting meeting at a products-liability and regulatory law firm representing a manufacturer of aircraft sensor-conditioning modules used in an electronics-rich analog control system. Opposing counsel has challenged the admissibility and reliability of the client’s internal fault-isolation analysis, which used a Gaussian-Bernoulli deep belief network to distinguish component degradation modes in two analog filter subcircuits from raw voltage/current traces. The immediate problem is that the draft expert declaration and accompanying exhibit package are being criticized as 'not reproducible' and 'insufficiently tied to the actual failure event.' The meeting agenda is to diagnose why the current evidentiary package is vulnerable, identify the root cause of the mismatch between the technical analysis and the legal record, and choose a corrective path before a hearing on a motion to exclude. The expected outcome is a concrete plan for what must be supplemented in the record, what additional validation should be prepared, and what materials will be referenced in the revised filing.

members.name: Evelyn Park
members.expertise: Products liability, expert-witness preparation, evidentiary foundations for technical exhibits, Daubert-style admissibility challenges
members.background: Evelyn is a seventh-year associate at a national law firm who manages expert reports and technical appendices in high-stakes engineering disputes. She is comfortable with engineering testimony at a high level but thinks primarily in terms of record foundation, chain of custody, and what can survive hostile cross-examination.
members.private_state: She wants a fast, defensible patch to the declaration that avoids reopening discovery or expanding the expert’s opinions beyond what has already been disclosed. She is worried that any mention of broader model development materials could invite a demand for more source material and more depositions.
hidden_assumptions: If an analysis is described as 'validated,' it should mean validated in the litigation sense: documented, fixed, and tied to materials already in the evidentiary record.
The 'test set' relevant to the court is the event-specific bench replay and exemplars generated for this case, not the model-development holdout data used internally by engineers months earlier.
A 'fix' to the admissibility problem means adding enough foundation and explanation to defend the existing opinion without materially enlarging the scope of production.
When the expert says the model used 'raw signals,' the important point is that the signals came from traceable, preserved instruments associated with the incident and follow-on bench reconstruction.

members.name: Daniel Rios
members.expertise: Electrical engineering, patent and technical litigation support, machine-learning-assisted diagnostics, failure analysis documentation
members.background: Daniel has an EE background and previously worked in reliability engineering before attending law school. At the firm he translates technical analyses for litigation teams and works closely with experts on explaining model architecture, validation practice, and fault-isolation workflows.
members.private_state: He wants to preserve the credibility of the technical methodology and fears that oversimplifying the model’s development process will make the analysis look weaker than it is. He is also concerned that the real weakness is not the method itself but the mismatch between legal drafting and engineering documentation.
hidden_assumptions: If an analysis is described as 'validated,' it means statistically validated on held-out fault classes and operating-condition variations in the engineering sense, even if every development artifact is not yet in the court filing.
The 'test set' naturally refers to the frozen holdout dataset used after model training, because that is standard terminology in ML-supported diagnostics.

A 'fix' to the problem means closing the reproducibility gap by documenting model version, preprocessing pipeline, and training/validation protocol, even if that adds technical detail and attachments.

When discussing 'raw signals,' he assumes everyone understands this means minimally processed digitized waveforms before handcrafted feature extraction, not necessarily incident-only traces or a single chain-of-custody packet.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to 'the test set' as the dataset that should support the declaration
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the event-linked bench replay files and exemplar traces generated during post-incident testing for this lawsuit, because those are the materials she assumes can be cleanly tied to the specific disputed failure.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the ML holdout dataset reserved during model development across known fault classes and operating conditions, because that is the standard technical meaning of test set in diagnostic model validation.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are accustomed to saying 'test set' without qualification in their own professional contexts, and the phrase sounds precise enough that neither expects it to be ambiguous in a troubleshooting meeting.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree they need to shore up the 'validation package' before the hearing
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes the package includes only the pieces necessary to authenticate the expert’s conclusions in the existing record: a clearer declaration, selected exhibits, and references to preserved bench tests already produced.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes the package should include broader technical materials necessary for engineering reproducibility, such as preprocessing steps, model versioning notes, architecture parameters, confusion matrices, and operating-condition coverage summaries.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'validation package' sounds like ordinary case-prep shorthand, and both think the omitted details are obviously encompassed by the same bucket even though each imagines a different boundary around it.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say they want a 'fix' that makes the analysis defensible
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks the problem is fixed if the judge can see a stable chain from preserved testing materials to the expert’s opinion without opening new disputes about discovery scope or undisclosed bases.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks the problem is fixed if a technically trained reviewer could reproduce the classification result and see why GB-DBN outperformed time-domain and frequency-domain features on the relevant analog filter faults.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: They both use the same high-level legal phrase—'defensible'—and each assumes the other shares the obvious standard for defensibility from their own discipline.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both discuss grounding the opinion in 'raw voltage and current signals'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 presupposes these are the preserved incident-related captures and the directly corresponding bench reconstruction traces that can be authenticated through custodian testimony.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 presupposes this includes the larger bank of minimally processed waveform captures from prior validation runs on the two analog filter circuits, regardless of whether each file has already been individually introduced into the litigation record.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Neither sees any reason to spell out the provenance of 'raw signals' because the phrase feels technical and concrete; the hidden gap is about legal record status, not signal format, so surface conversation does not naturally expose it.

turns.inner_thought: The judge's concern is not that the expert changed his mind; it's that the declaration reads like a black box. I need a fast patch that makes the existing opinion look fixed, documented, and tied to what is already in the record. If we can tighten the chain from preserved incident-related testing and bench reconstruction to the opinion, we can survive without inviting requests for broader development material or reopening discovery.
